problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-{3}^{x}+1?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={3}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/17a76468bd4f446f420d784ae479724135b2af3369a7d69f87c67507e74a8901.png)

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{3}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/ac5e769c069b753bbf3f6a9a276b69881a3d2699afc4f62498233ecc526f5a2b.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $1$ unit up to give $y=-{3}^{x}+1.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(0,0)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/c69c8be5828709cef483cba56d5842b973cf718e7592a8fba9e825be08204f5b.png)
